intro: Ten franchises, ten different questions. Each study starts from what actually happened on the field in recent seasons, sets it against what the StatEdge outlook sees for the 2027 squad, and ends with the one thing a decision-maker should check first.

cases.headline: The team that qualifies, until it doesn't
cases.dek: Four playoffs in five seasons, one year at the bottom of the league, and five more wins than their runs deserve. Which Gujarat should a franchise believe?
cases.question: Gujarat have reached the playoffs in four of their five seasons. Does that make them a safe bet to qualify again in 2027?

evidence.title: The record is real, and it swings hard
evidence.body: Measured in runs per match above or below the league average that season, Gujarat went +6, +36, -25, +17, +35. The one miss, 2024, came at -25: the lowest reading in the league that year.

evidence.title: Strength rarely repeats in the IPL
evidence.body: Across every franchise and season in the data, a team's strength one year explains almost nothing of the next (a correlation of 0.08 over 145 season pairs). Gujarat's record is context, not a forecast.

evidence.title: Where the 2027 squad is exposed
evidence.body: The batting looks strong in the powerplay and middle overs, but the outlook rates the bowling in the middle and death overs as the weak side. Five overseas players (Buttler, Rashid Khan, Holder, Phillips and Rabada) compete for four places in the XI. On the last two years of form StatEdge leaves Rashid Khan out: his middle-over economy is 8.2 and his death economy close to 11.

evidence.title: A top-heavy batting order
evidence.body: In StatEdge's XI the top three batters score about 62% of the team's runs, the highest share of any team in the league. Qualifying sides do lean on their top three, but 62% means one early wicket changes the innings.

cases.insight: Gujarat are a good example of why a track record and a squad audit answer different questions. The record says 'usually qualifies'. The squad audit says 'four overseas slots, one thin bowling unit and a very top-heavy order'. The outlook lands below the middle of the table, and it is not saying they will miss; it is saying the margin for error is smaller than the record suggests.
watch: Which four of the five overseas players start, and whether Rashid Khan is one of them
Who bowls the death overs: the bowling plan relies on very few proven options there
How much the top three carry again; a quiet powerplay is the main way this side falls over
cases.takeaway: A strong record earns a seat at the table, but the 2027 case rests on the bowling squad, not the history.

deep.short_answer: Gujarat are a good team whose record runs a little ahead of their run totals, and whose batting leans on three men. Both points matter more than the playoff streak.
deep.why: A 14-match season is short enough that two or three close results can decide a playoff place. Knowing whether a record comes from strength or from fortunate finishes tells a franchise how far to trust it when it picks a squad.

analysis.title: The record nobody argues with
analysis.simple: Net run rate is the runs a team scores per over minus the runs it concedes per over. It is how the IPL breaks ties on points.
body: Gujarat won 10, 10, 5, 9 and 9 games in their five seasons. Four of those years ended in the playoffs. The fifth, 2024, ended at 5 wins and 7 defeats with a net run rate of −0.91, the one year the run totals and the table agreed that Gujarat were ordinary.
That is the record. The next question is whether the runs behind it agree.

analysis.title: Then check the receipts
analysis.lead: A record is one thing. The runs behind it are another.
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from the runs it scores and concedes. They are fitted on every IPL season since 2008, so they describe the league, not Gujarat.
body: From 2022 to 2026 Gujarat won 43 of 68 league games (63%). Their runs scored and conceded point to 38.0 wins, so they won 5.0 more than the numbers predict. A typical team's gap in one season is about 1.4 wins either way, which adds up to roughly 3.0 over five seasons. Gujarat's gap is above that usual spread without being off the chart.
Take 2025. Gujarat scored 191.7 runs a match and conceded 189.1, a margin of only 2.6. A margin that thin usually earns about 7.4 wins. Gujarat won 9 of 14.

analysis.title: How they win: chase it, anywhere
analysis.lead: If the runs are not the whole story, what is?
analysis.simple: Chasing teams win a little more than half of IPL matches, so only a clear gap means anything. Home form uses the ground where the team played most of its matches that season.
body: Gujarat won 25 of 37 chases (68%) against 18 of 31 when batting first (58%). Across the league, chasing sides won 56%. It is a real edge, and also a reminder that Gujarat win by hitting a target more reliably than by setting one.

They do not need the Narendra Modi Stadium to do it. At home they won 16 of 27 (59%). Away from it they won 17 of 27 (63%). A team that wins as often away as at home is not leaning on conditions it knows.

analysis.title: Three men and a long tail
analysis.lead: Now look at who scores the runs.
analysis.simple: Top-three run share is the share of the team's runs scored by its three highest run-scorers. A high number means the order is top-heavy.
body: In 2026 Gujarat's top three of B Sai Sudharsan, Shubman Gill and JC Buttler scored 71% of the team's runs. The league average that season was 54%. (The 62% quoted in the original finding is the share projected for the 2027 XI; this is what actually happened in 2026.) The fourth-highest scorer, Washington Sundar, made 303.

A trio like that is a gift while all three are fit and scoring, and a risk when they are not. In the league's history, playoff teams do lean on their top three more than other teams, so concentration alone is not a flaw.

analysis.title: A careful start
analysis.lead: One more thing the record hides.
analysis.simple: Runs per over compared with the league average, over all IPL league matches in 2024 to 2026. A gap of 0.5 runs an over is 3 runs across the six powerplay overs.
body: Gujarat's powerplay batting scored 8.91 an over against a league 9.74, about 5.0 runs a match fewer, with only 22% of balls going for four or six against 26% for the league. They lose very few wickets there (2.8 per 100 balls, league 4.3). It is a careful start, not a fast one.
Their best phase on the other side is the powerplay bowling: 9.28 an over against 9.74, ranked 1 of 10, with 5.0 wickets per 100 balls against 4.3.

history: 2022 and 2023: 10 wins each year, with net run rates of +0.13 then +0.74. The 2023 side scored 8.9 runs a match more than it conceded and was the strongest in the league by that measure.
2024: 5 wins and 7 defeats, net run rate −0.91. Unlike the other years, this season matched the run totals (5.3 expected wins), so the miss was a genuine one, not bad luck.
2025 and 2026: 9 wins each year, net run rates of +0.29 and +0.32. Over the five seasons Gujarat finished above expectation in 4 years and below it in 1.

matches.why: On 08 Apr 2026 Gujarat made 210/4 and beat Delhi by a single run, 210 to 209. The top score was Shubman Gill 70 (45) and the best bowling Rashid Khan 3/17. Turn that one run around and 2026 reads 8-6 instead of 9-5, a thin margin to hang a playoff place on.
matches.heading: Won by one run

matches.why: The same team, in the same season, was bowled out for 100 chasing 200 against Mumbai, twelve days after that one-run win. This is the other side of a top-three batting order: when it fails, the rest of the innings does not rescue it.
matches.heading: Lost by 99 runs, twelve days later

matches.why: A month later Gujarat made 229/4 against Chennai; the top score was B Sai Sudharsan 84 (53). When the top three fire, Gujarat win very big.
matches.heading: Won by 89 runs

matches.why: The year Gujarat missed the playoffs, Delhi bowled them out for 89 and chased it down with six wickets in hand. Collapses like this are what a careful start with a thin middle can lead to.
matches.heading: All out for 89

hidden.title: The projection and the record disagree about the powerplay
body: The 2027 outlook rates Gujarat's powerplay batting as a strength, but the last three seasons of actual play show below-average scoring there. One possible reason is that the projection is built from the current squad's individual records while the team record reflects how the order was actually used. The data cannot confirm that, so treat it as a question to check.

hidden.title: Rashid Khan's 2026 was fine; the worry is the two-year window
body: In 2026 Rashid Khan took 19 wickets at 8.72 an over from 48 overs, which is a respectable season. The outlook leaves him out because it weighs two years of form, not one.

hidden.title: The death-over question runs through Siraj
body: Mohammed Siraj bowled 11 death overs in 2026 at 11.82 an over and gave away 0.55 wides and no-ball runs per over; K Rabada went for 9.20 with 0.20. The league gives away 0.49 extras an over at the death.

counter.q: Is five seasons enough to say Gujarat over-perform their run totals?
counter.a: Not conclusively. Five seasons is 68 matches, and the usual spread of the five-season gap is about 3.0 wins. Gujarat's is 5.0. It leans toward 'fortunate' but does not prove it.

counter.q: Could the three-batter concentration be a strength, not a weakness?
counter.a: Yes. In the league's history, playoff teams lean on their top three more than other teams do. Concentration helps when the top three are this good. The risk only shows on the days they fail, like the all-out 100.

counter.q: Does the 2027 outlook change the story?
counter.a: The outlook is a projection for a changed squad. Where it disagrees with the record (the powerplay), treat it as a question to check, not an answer.

implications: Decide which four of the five overseas players start by looking at the bowling: the batting already has depth at the top, while the death overs are the thinnest unit.
Give the fourth and fifth batters a defined role. With 71% of the runs coming from three men, the next two batters decide the innings on the days the top three fail.
Review the powerplay approach: scoring 5.0 runs a match fewer than the league in the first six overs is the cost of a careful start.
Track the chase: the best-performing part of the record, and the part most likely to move back toward the league's 56%.
deep.verdict: Believe the chasing and the bowling early in the innings. Price the record a little below what it looks like. Gujarat are a good side whose results have run slightly ahead of their runs and whose batting rests on three players. Qualifying again is plausible; assuming it is not.
deep.data_note: League-stage IPL matches only (playoffs excluded). Team and player figures use 2022 to 2026; the expected-wins fit uses every season since 2008 (153 team-seasons). Phase comparisons use the last three seasons, 2024 to 2026. Close matches are those decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer.
deep.hook: Gujarat Titans have reached the playoffs in four of their five IPL seasons. In the fifth, 2024, they were the weakest team in the league by runs scored and wickets lost. Over those same five seasons they won 5 more games than the runs they scored and conceded say they should have. So which Gujarat should a franchise believe: the one that keeps qualifying, or the one the scoreboard describes?

analysis: Five findings. Each is explained in plain terms first, then with the numbers.
history: Season by season
The same story told one year at a time, with what the runs say each record should have been.
matches: Four nights that tell the story
Picked by a fixed rule from the ball-by-ball record: the closest win, the heaviest defeat, a big win and a collapse.
hidden: Three things that only show up when you look inside the numbers.
counter: The strongest objections to the conclusion, and how well it holds up.
implications: What a franchise should do with this
Each point connects to a finding above.

cases.headline: Best squad on paper, bouncing results
cases.dek: Five titles, the top spot in the 2027 outlook, and a recent record that jumps 50 runs a match from one year to the next.
cases.question: Mumbai top the 2027 outlook, yet they missed the playoffs in three of the last five seasons. Is the outlook wrong, or is the record misleading?

evidence.title: A record that bounces
evidence.body: Mumbai's season strength reads -27, +1, -17, +31, -23 since 2022. The jump from +31 (2025) to -23 (2026) is a 53-run swing per match, with the same group of players available.

evidence.title: Nothing changed to explain it
evidence.body: All eleven players in StatEdge's 2027 XI played for Mumbai last season. When the roster does not move and the results still do, the variance is not coming from turnover. It is the ordinary noise of a 14-match season.

evidence.title: What the outlook sees
evidence.body: The strongest unit in StatEdge's XI is batting at the death (6.5 out of 10), with the middle-overs batting above the league average too. The weakest phases are bowling at the death (4.2) and in the powerplay (5.0), even with Bumrah in the side.

evidence.title: How big is the lead, really?
evidence.body: Mumbai are first with a 57% playoff chance and a 16% title chance, about nine points ahead of second place on the playoffs. Even the favourite misses the playoffs more than four times in ten.

cases.insight: The useful read is not 'Mumbai are favourites'. It is 'Mumbai are the team whose lower-tier years are most likely to be bad luck rather than bad squads'. The outlook is built around the players in the squad, not the franchise's last results, which is why it does not follow the dip. That is a strength when the cause of a dip is noise and a weakness when the cause is something the data cannot see, such as an injury or a dressing-room issue.
watch: Death bowling beyond Bumrah: the second and third options decide the last five overs
Powerplay bowling: a weak phase for a side that depends on early control
Whether the batting order uses the strong death hitters early enough
cases.takeaway: A small edge on a very noisy sport: favourite, not certainty.

deep.short_answer: Mumbai's results have fallen below their run totals in four of five seasons, which supports the idea that part of the dip is bad luck. But 2026 was also a genuinely poor year for batting first.
deep.why: A franchise that reads a bad season as a bad squad may break up a side that was only unlucky. Separating the two protects against over-reacting in the auction and in selection.

analysis.title: Wins against what the runs say
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from the runs it scores and concedes, fitted on every IPL season since 2008.
body: Across 2022 to 2026 Mumbai won 28 of 70 league games, while their runs point to 33.2. That is a gap of -5.2 wins, and they finished below expectation in 4 of the five seasons. The usual spread over five seasons is about 3.0 wins, so Mumbai's gap is at the edge of what chance alone produces.
In 2024 they scored 183.4 a match and conceded 190.0, a deficit of 6.6 runs. That usually earns about 6.0 wins; they won 4.

analysis.title: A real problem when batting first
analysis.simple: Win rate when setting a target, compared with when chasing.
body: In 2026 Mumbai won 1 of 7 matches when batting first and 3 of 7 when chasing. Over five seasons the figures are 34% batting first and 44% chasing, against a league chasing win rate of 56%. Batting first has been the weaker half.

analysis.title: Strong at home, weak away
analysis.simple: Win rate at the ground where the team played most of its matches that season, against all other grounds.
body: At Wankhede Mumbai won 15 of 28 (54%) from 2023 to 2026. Elsewhere they won 9 of 28 (32%). Home form has kept the record respectable, and the away record is where the season is lost.

analysis.title: No single phase is broken
analysis.simple: Runs a match above or below the league average, by phase, over 2024 to 2026.
body: The phase table shows no big gap in either direction. The largest is powerplay batting at −2.3 runs a match against the league. The best is death bowling, where Mumbai concede 1.5 runs a match fewer than the league and take 9.3 wickets per 100 balls (league 8.2), ranked 2 of 10. In simple terms, Mumbai are an average team in every phase, with a sharper finish than start.

analysis.title: A bowling attack built around one man
analysis.simple: Economy rate is runs conceded per over. The league's death overs cost 11.00 runs an over.
body: In 2026 JJ Bumrah bowled 13 death overs at 8.15 an over. The other regular death bowlers went for 12.00 and 12.17. Across the whole 2026 season the next three wicket-takers conceded between 9.7 and 12.3 an over.

history: 2022: 4 wins and a net run rate of −0.56; run totals pointed to 5.4 wins.
2023 and 2025 were the playoff seasons: 8 and 8 wins. The 2025 side had the best run difference of the five (+0.82 net run rate, 9.0 expected wins) and was still a little unlucky.
2024 and 2026 each ended on 4 wins. The 2026 net run rate was −0.71 against +0.82 the year before.

matches.why: The 2026 season in one match: bowled out for 104 chasing 208. One result like this moves the season's run difference by several runs a match without costing more than a single win.
The same side chased 229 down with six wickets to spare. Both the heavy defeat and this win belong to 2026.
A 100-run win in 2025, when Mumbai had the best run difference of the five seasons.
Rickelton's 81 off 43 was the high point of Mumbai's powerplay batting in a 224-run chase.

hidden.title: Batting is spread, not top-heavy
body: Mumbai's top three scored 46% of the team's runs in 2026, against a league average of 54%. RD Rickelton made 448 runs at a strike rate of 187, Tilak Varma 359 at 146. The runs came from many hands, not a few.

hidden.title: Close matches do not explain it
body: Mumbai played only 7 close matches in five seasons (decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer) and won 2. The gap to expected wins comes from games that were not close.

counter.q: Could heavy defeats distort the run totals?
counter.a: Yes. A 103-run loss counts fully in runs conceded but only once in the table. Expected wins are sensitive to blowouts, which is one reason the gap should be read as a hint, not a verdict.

counter.q: Is the batting-first problem luck?
counter.a: Perhaps in part, but the pattern is wider than one year: 34% batting first over five seasons against 44% chasing.

counter.q: Does the outlook ignore Mumbai's history?
counter.a: It does. The outlook is built from what players do, not from franchise results, so it will not follow a run of bad years, and it cannot see injuries or dressing-room problems.

implications: Find a second reliable death bowler. The drop from 8.15 an over to 12.00 and beyond is the clearest weakness in the regular attack.
Plan for batting first: it is the weaker half of the record, and an extra bowling option can help defend a total.
Look at away-ground selection: the home record is respectable and the away record is where the table is lost.
Do not rebuild on one season: the run totals do not show a side as poor as the table did.
deep.verdict: Mumbai are an average-to-good side whose results have lagged their runs. They are the favourite in the outlook by a small margin, and the record gives no strong reason to doubt that.
deep.data_note: League-stage IPL matches only (playoffs excluded). Team and player figures use 2022 to 2026; the expected-wins fit uses every season since 2008 (153 team-seasons). Phase comparisons use the last three seasons, 2024 to 2026. Close matches are those decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer.

cases.headline: The 45-run champion who vanished
cases.dek: 2024 was the strongest season by any team in the last five years. The two seasons since have both missed the playoffs.
cases.question: How much of a championship season is repeatable?

evidence.title: An outlier season
evidence.body: In 2024 Kolkata finished 45 runs a match above the league average, with a 75% win rate, and won the title. No other team in the last five seasons reached +40.

evidence.title: Then back to the pack
evidence.body: 2025 and 2026 read -4 and -5: below average, 42% win rate each year, and no playoffs. Eleven of the eleven players in the 2027 XI were with the side last year, so this is not a clear-out.

evidence.title: What the data says should have happened
evidence.body: Over 19 seasons, a team's strength carries forward by roughly 0.08 per run. A +45 season predicts about +4 the next year. Kolkata's 2025 reading (-4) sits well inside the normal spread around that. The 2024 season was the surprise, not the decline.

evidence.title: What the outlook sees
evidence.body: The 2027 outlook rates Kolkata fifth: a 40% playoff chance. The standout is bowling at the death (8.4 out of 10, the best of any team), helped by the lowest wide and no-ball rate in the league at the death. The weak spot is the middle overs, in both batting and bowling.

cases.insight: Kolkata show why one standout season should not be extrapolated, and also why the death bowling matters: death-over extras were one of the few measures that cost teams beyond what runs and wickets already show. A side that holds its lines in the last five overs gets a real edge, and Kolkata's numbers there are the best in the league.
watch: The middle overs: both batting and bowling rate in the bottom half
Narine and Varun's workload; the spin core drives the phase that is weakest
Whether the death-bowling discipline holds when the opposition is aggressive
cases.takeaway: Expect a good team with one elite phase, not a repeat of 2024.

deep.short_answer: Kolkata's 2024 title season was supported by the runs, not by luck, and the decline since is also supported by the runs. The side that remains is an ordinary team that is excellent at the death.
deep.why: A title winner's next seasons tell a franchise how much of a great year was repeatable. Kolkata are a clean test, because the margin in 2024 was so large and the fall since so clear.

analysis.title: 2024 was real
analysis.simple: Net run rate is runs scored per over minus runs conceded per over across a season.
body: In 2024 Kolkata scored 199.1 a match and conceded 177.9, a margin of 21.2 runs and a net run rate of +1.12. They won 9 of 12. Those runs point to 8.5 wins, so the title season was not a lucky one. The side was simply that good.

analysis.title: The decline is also real
analysis.simple: If a fall were bad luck, run totals would still look strong. Here they do not.
body: In 2025 the margin was −6.7 runs a match and in 2026 −8.4. Both years ended with 5 wins, and the runs point to 5.1 and 4.9. The record matches the run totals almost exactly, so the fall is a return to the pack, not a run of bad breaks.

analysis.title: The death overs are the real edge
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league over 2024 to 2026, with the death overs being overs 16 to 20.
body: Kolkata concede 10.17 an over at the death against a league 11.00, which is 4.2 runs a match fewer, the best in the league (rank 1 of 10). They take 9.9 wickets per 100 balls (league 8.2) and 35% of death balls are dots against 28%.

analysis.title: Narine at the death
analysis.simple: Economy rate is runs conceded per over; lower is better.
body: In 2026 SP Narine bowled 9 death overs at 5.44 an over with 9 wickets. Kartik Tyagi bowled 20 death overs at 10.60 with 9 wickets. Both are well below the league's 11.00.

history: 2022 and 2023: 6 wins each year. In 2022 Kolkata lost all 3 of their close matches.
2024: 9 wins and the title, with a chase record of 3 from 3.
2025 and 2026: 5 wins each, with a net run rate of −0.23 and +0.02.

matches.venue: Andhra Cricket Association-Visakhapatnam District Cricket Association Stadium
matches.why: Narine made 85 off 39 in a 272-run total, a 106-run win over Delhi in 2024: the kind of match that builds a season margin of 21 runs.
A one-run win in 2025. Narrow results like this are where small differences in luck show up.
A 278-run total against them in 2025 and a 110-run defeat: the other side of the same margin story.

matches.note: Fewest runs conceded in a full set of death overs since 2022
matches.why: Russell took 3 for 22 as Kolkata held Sunrisers to 123 in 2022, a death-over defence of the kind the record rewards.

hidden.title: History and outlook disagree about the middle overs
body: Kolkata's actual middle-over bowling from 2024 to 2026 saved 4.2 runs a match against the league (8.62 an over against 9.09), while the 2027 outlook rates that unit weak. The two views point in opposite directions, and this data cannot say why; changes to the squad are one possible reason.

hidden.title: The batting is the problem in the middle
body: Their middle-over batting scored 8.81 an over against a league 9.09, with 17% of balls going for four or six against 18%.

counter.q: Was 2024 special because of one thing?
counter.a: The data shows a very large run margin (21.2 a match) but cannot show why. We do not see opening partnerships or lineup changes here.

counter.q: Does the decline prove regression to the mean?
counter.a: It fits it. A season at the top of the league rarely repeats: across the league's history, a strong season explains only a small share of the next one.

counter.q: Is three seasons enough to judge the death bowling?
counter.a: It is a real signal (4.2 runs a match), but bowling units change, and death-over figures depend on a few bowlers.

implications: Protect the death-over edge: two or three bowlers account for it, so depth there is cheap insurance.
Fix the middle-over batting: it scores 2.5 runs a match fewer than the league.
Do not plan on a repeat of 2024: the run totals say the side has been an ordinary team since.
deep.verdict: Kolkata won a title with a real margin and have been average-to-poor since, apart from an excellent death attack. The right expectation is a mid-table side with one elite phase.
deep.data_note: League-stage IPL matches only (playoffs excluded). Team and player figures use 2022 to 2026; the expected-wins fit uses every season since 2008 (153 team-seasons). Phase comparisons use the last three seasons, 2024 to 2026. Close matches are those decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer.

cases.headline: Seven wins, seven losses, no playoffs
cases.dek: Chennai were above average in 2024 and still missed out. Short seasons are crueller than they look.
cases.question: Chennai have missed the playoffs three years running. Is that a sign of decline, or of a hard-to-read sport?

evidence.title: A decent side that missed
evidence.body: In 2024 Chennai scored 8.5 runs a match above the league average and finished 7 and 7. That was good enough for a better record in many other years, and not enough that season.

evidence.title: A 14-match season is short
evidence.body: A team that is truly average still wins between 5 and 9 of its 14 games about four times in five. The league table can hide a real gap in quality or invent one.

evidence.title: The last two years: one weak, one near average
evidence.body: 2025 was clearly weak (-12, a 29% win rate). 2026 was close to average (-4, a 43% win rate). Missing out twice in a row is not the same as being a poor side twice in a row.

evidence.title: What the outlook sees
evidence.body: Chennai rate seventh with a 39% playoff chance. They are strongest where the game is slowest: bowling in the middle overs (7.5 out of 10) and batting in the same phase (6.1). They are weakest in the powerplay bowling (3.3) and the death bowling (3.9), the two phases where the ball does the most damage.

cases.insight: Chennai's squad is built for control: it is strong when the game is slow and exposed when it is fast. The data points to a specific fix, not a rebuild: a bowler who can take wickets in the powerplay and a second reliable option for the death overs.
watch: A new-ball option that can take wickets in the powerplay
The identity of the second death bowler behind the first
How the top order handles the powerplay
cases.takeaway: Middle of the table, with a clear and fixable shape.

deep.short_answer: Chennai have won far fewer games than their run totals suggest in four of five seasons. They have been a better team than their table position, and their middle-over batting has been the weakest in the league.
deep.why: Missing the playoffs three years in a row looks like decline. If the run totals say otherwise, it points a franchise at converting, not rebuilding.

analysis.title: A persistent gap between runs and wins
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from the runs it scores and concedes, fitted on every IPL season since 2008.
body: Across 2022 to 2026 Chennai won 29 of 69 league games, while their runs point to 37.6. That is 8.6 fewer wins than expected. The usual spread of the five-season gap is about 3.0 wins, so Chennai's gap is nearly three times the usual spread, a rare size.
In 2024 they scored 180.3 a match and conceded 172.5, a margin of 7.8 runs, and finished 7 and 7. The runs point to 8.2 wins and a playoff place.

analysis.title: It is not close-match luck
analysis.simple: A close match is one decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer.
body: Chennai played only 6 close matches in five seasons and won 2. The shortfall is not coming from coin-flip finishes. It is coming from games that were lost by a distance, which count fully in run totals but only once in the table.

analysis.title: Weak both ways around
analysis.simple: Win rate when batting first and when chasing, over five seasons.
body: Chennai won 16 of 40 batting first (40%) and 13 of 29 chasing (45%). The league's chasing teams won 56%. Neither half of the record is strong.

analysis.title: The middle overs are the problem
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league average, over 2024 to 2026. The middle overs are 7 to 15.
body: Chennai's middle-over batting scored 8.37 an over against 9.09, which is 6.5 runs a match fewer, the lowest in the league (rank 10 of 10). Only 15% of balls went for four or six, against 18%.
Their middle-over bowling, by contrast, is excellent: 8.50 against 9.09, saving 5.3 runs a match. The control Chennai bowl with in the middle overs is not matched by the batting.

analysis.title: Few wickets early
analysis.simple: Wickets per 100 balls, a measure of how often a bowling side takes a wicket.
body: Chennai take 3.4 wickets per 100 balls in the powerplay against 4.3 for the league, the lowest rate of any team (rank 10 of 10). Their new-ball attack contains runs but rarely takes wickets.

history: 2022: 4 wins with a margin of +2.4 runs a match. The runs point to 7.4 wins; the season was 3.4 wins short of that.
2023, the title year: 8 wins, a net run rate of +0.65, almost exactly what the runs predicted.
2024: 7 and 7 despite a net run rate of +0.35. 2025: 4 wins and a net run rate of −0.68, a weak season by the runs as well. 2026: 6 wins, −0.14.

An 89-run defeat to Gujarat in 2026, bowled out for 140 chasing 230.
A 103-run win over Mumbai in the same season: Samson 101 off 54. Chennai can win big as well as lose big.

hidden.title: The outlook and the record disagree about the middle overs
body: The 2027 outlook rates Chennai's middle-over batting above average, but the last three seasons were the league's lowest by runs per over. The outlook is built from current players, and the record is from the order they played. The data cannot say which will prove right, so the middle-over batting is the first thing to check.

counter.q: Could the run-difference gap just be a few blowouts?
counter.a: Partly. Heavy defeats like the Lost by 89 runs in 2026 count fully in runs conceded and only once in the table. We cannot tell from this data whether the heavy defeats are bad luck or a sign of how the team collapses.

counter.q: Is a weak middle-over record about the order and not the players?
counter.a: It could be. The record cannot separate player quality from how they were used.

counter.q: Does missing the playoffs prove decline?
counter.a: Not by the runs: the 2024 side scored well above what it conceded.

implications: Treat middle-over batting as the first problem: it scores 6.5 runs a match fewer than the league.
Add a powerplay wicket-taker: Chennai take the fewest early wickets in the league.
Do not rebuild a bowling attack that saves 5.3 runs a match in the middle overs; fix the phases around it.
Review how heavy defeats happen: they cost runs conceded but not extra table points.
deep.verdict: Chennai have been better than their table positions, and the problem is specific: middle-over batting and early wickets. A mid-table outlook is fair, with room to move up if the batting phase is fixed.

cases.headline: The one team whose strength actually repeats
cases.dek: Four straight seasons well above average, back-to-back titles, and the only side in the league to do it.
cases.question: If strength rarely repeats, how has Bengaluru stayed at the top for four seasons?

evidence.title: A steady line in a noisy league
evidence.body: Bengaluru's season strength reads +15, +10, +9 and +11 over the last four seasons. Every other team in the league swung by 30 runs or more across those years; Bengaluru stayed within about 6.

evidence.title: The results followed
evidence.body: Playoffs in four of the last five years, 64% to 69% win rates in the last two, and titles in 2025 and 2026.

evidence.title: One miss that was luck
evidence.body: In 2023 Bengaluru were 15 runs a match above average and still missed the playoffs. With a 50% win rate, they were eliminated by results that could have gone either way.

evidence.title: What the outlook sees
evidence.body: Third, with a 44% playoff chance. The outlook credits the powerplay bowling (6.5 out of 10) and the batting at the death (5.9). The middle overs are the weak phase: bowling there rates 3.0, the lowest middle-overs bowling score in the league.

cases.insight: Because strength rarely repeats, Bengaluru's streak is the most informative thing in the data: holding a high level for four seasons in a league where that almost never happens is worth studying. The outlook's probability (44%) is more modest than the record, which is the honest position: the streak is evidence of quality, not a guarantee.
watch: Middle-over bowling: the lowest-rated unit in the XI
Whether the middle overs can be protected without costing the powerplay edge
Top-order reliance: the top three score about 54% of runs
cases.takeaway: The benchmark for what a durable squad looks like.

deep.short_answer: Bengaluru have been a consistently good side, but their last two seasons' wins ran ahead of their run totals, so the record flatters them a little. The dependable part is the death overs, both batting and bowling.
deep.why: A franchise whose strength truly repeats is rare in this league. Checking what lies under the streak shows what to keep.

analysis.title: A steady margin, a luckier record
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from runs scored and conceded, fitted on every IPL season since 2008.
body: Bengaluru's net run rate was +0.31 in 2024, +0.31 in 2025 and +0.68 in 2026, a steady and positive line. In 2025 and 2026 they won 9 and 9 games against expectations of 6.9 and 7.3, a combined 2.1 plus 1.7 extra wins.

analysis.title: Winning away
analysis.simple: Win rate at the ground where the team played most of its matches that season against all other grounds.
body: In 2025 Bengaluru won 7 of 8 away games and 2 of 5 at home. In 2026 it was 4 of 5 at home and 5 of 9 away.

analysis.title: The finish is their strength on both sides
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league over 2024 to 2026; the death overs are 16 to 20.
body: At the death Bengaluru's batting scored 11.89 an over against 11.00, which is 4.5 runs a match more, with 28% of balls going for four or six against 24%. Their death bowling conceded 10.59 against 11.00, saving 2.1 runs a match.

analysis.title: The middle overs leak
analysis.simple: Runs conceded per over against the league average; a higher number is worse.
body: Bengaluru's middle-over bowling conceded 9.46 an over against 9.09, which is 3.4 runs a match more than the league and ranks 10 of 10. They also take fewer wickets there (4.3 per 100 balls, league 4.6).

analysis.title: Less dependent on one man
analysis.simple: Share of the team's runs scored by one player.
body: V Kohli scored 708 runs in 2024, 27% of the team's total. In 2026 he made 557, 22%, and D Padikkal and RM Patidar added 433 and 393.

history: 2022: 8 wins. 2023: 7 wins and a net run rate of −0.18, about what the runs predicted.
2024: 7 wins with a margin of 8.0 runs a match and 8.2 expected. They were unlucky by 1.2 wins.
2025 and 2026: 9 wins each year, ahead of expectations, and two titles.

matches.why: A 112-run win in 2023 that dismissed Rajasthan for 59.
A one-run defeat in 2024: bowled out for 221 chasing 222. A close result that cost a point of expected wins but not a point of run totals.
92 for 1 in the powerplay chasing 148: du Plessis 64 off 23. The kind of start that makes a chase easy.

matches.note: Most runs conceded in overs 16-20 since 2022
matches.why: Chennai scored 83 in the death overs in 2022, the heaviest leak of the five seasons.

hidden.title: A home-ground paradox
body: In 2025 Bengaluru were better away from home than at it (7 of 8 away, 2 of 5 at home). A year later the pattern reversed. The sample is small, so the split is probably noise.

hidden.title: Top-heavy, but at the league's level
body: The 2026 top-three share was 55% against a league average of 54%.

counter.q: Is the streak partly fortune?
counter.a: Yes: two seasons of finishing ahead of expectation. But the margins stayed positive every year, so the strength is not an illusion.

counter.q: Do two titles prove sustained dominance?
counter.a: No. The run margins are good rather than dominant, and the league's history shows that titles carry a large element of luck.

counter.q: Can the middle-over leak be fixed without losing the death edge?
counter.a: The data cannot say. The two phases use different bowlers in different roles.

implications: Keep the death-over core in both batting and bowling: it is worth more than 4.5 runs a match.
Fix the middle-over bowling: it concedes 3.4 runs a match more than the league.
Treat the last two seasons' wins as slightly flattering when planning squad strength.
deep.verdict: Bengaluru's strength has genuinely repeated, with a slightly flattering last two years. A repeat is plausible, not assured, and the middle overs are the place to improve.

cases.headline: Great bowling at the death, nothing at the start
cases.dek: From +13 in 2022 to -26 in 2026, with a bowling attack that peaks late.
cases.question: Lucknow began with two playoff seasons and have missed three in a row since. What changed in the shape of the side?

evidence.title: A long downward drift
evidence.body: Lucknow's season strength reads +13, +6, -20, -10 and -26 across 2022 to 2026, and the win rate fell to 31% in 2026. The two playoff seasons were the first two.

evidence.title: The outlook is not as bleak as the record
evidence.body: Lucknow rate ninth of ten, with a 28% playoff chance. That is below the middle but well short of a certain miss.

evidence.title: A bowling attack that peaks late
evidence.body: The death overs (7.1 out of 10) and middle overs (6.3) are the best phases by a wide margin. The powerplay is the weakest bowling phase of any team in the league (2.7), and the batting in the middle overs (3.1) is the second weak spot.

evidence.title: The shape of the problem
evidence.body: A bowling unit that is strong late and weak early starts every innings behind. Against sides that score heavily in the powerplay, the death bowlers are defending a total that has already got away.

cases.insight: Lucknow are a specific, solvable case: a squad that mainly needs a powerplay option and middle-order batting, not a rebuild. The data points to one signing priority (a powerplay wicket-taker) and one tactical question (whether the order protects the middle overs).
watch: A powerplay bowler who takes wickets, not just contains
Who anchors the middle overs
Whether the death-over strength is carried by one bowler or several
cases.takeaway: A late-overs team that needs to fix the start.

deep.short_answer: Lucknow's slide shows up in the run totals as well as the table: they have conceded more runs than they scored in each of the last three seasons. The bowling gives runs away in all three phases, and takes the fewest wickets at the death.
deep.why: A franchise needs to know whether its early success was real strength before it decides how much to change.

analysis.title: Conceding more than scoring
analysis.simple: Runs margin is the difference between runs scored and runs conceded per match.
body: From 2024 to 2026 Lucknow's margin was −2.7, −3.4 and −8.1 runs a match, with net run rates of −0.60, −0.38 and −0.70. In 2022 and 2023 it was +4.7 and +2.8.

analysis.title: The early playoff seasons were helped by luck
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from runs scored and conceded.
body: In 2022 Lucknow won 9 games against 7.8 expected, and in 2023 8 against 6.9. They won 4 of 6 close matches in 2023. The early record was real but a little flattered.

analysis.title: A bowling attack that leaks in every phase
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league average over 2024 to 2026. Positive means worse than the league.
body: Lucknow's bowling conceded 1.2 runs a match more than the league in the powerplay, 2.6 in the middle overs and 2.2 at the death. At the death they take 6.8 wickets per 100 balls against 8.2, the lowest of any team (rank 10 of 10), and only 26% of death balls are dots against 28%.

analysis.title: A batting order that has also dipped
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league over 2024 to 2026.
body: Lucknow's batting scored 2.2 runs a match fewer than the league in the powerplay and 3.0 fewer at the death.

analysis.title: Setting targets used to be the strength
analysis.simple: Win rate when batting first compared with chasing.
body: In 2022 Lucknow won 7 of 8 when batting first. In 2026 it was 1 of 8, while they won 3 of 5 chasing.

history: 2022 and 2023: 9 and 8 wins, both playoff seasons.
2024: 7 wins and a net run rate of −0.60. 2025: 6 wins, −0.38.
2026: 4 wins from 13, a net run rate of −0.70 and 5.4 expected wins.

matches.venue: Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium
matches.why: A 98-run defeat in 2024, bowled out for 137 chasing 236. Kolkata scored 64 in the death overs.
A powerplay of 91 for 1 and a score of 203 in 2026, and still a five-wicket defeat. Fast starts do not win games when the bowling cannot hold the total.
A 75-run win in 2022, when Lucknow set targets and defended them.
A three-run loss in 2022 that Rajasthan took with 73 in the death overs.

hidden.title: Reliance has eased
body: In 2024 Lucknow's top three scored 60% of the team's runs, led by KL Rahul and N Pooran. In 2026 it was 48%, with MR Marsh making 563 runs.

body: In 2026 Prince Yadav bowled 17 death overs at 9.82 an over. Mohammed Shami went for 13.33.

counter.q: Is the run margin affected by a few heavy defeats?
counter.a: Possibly. Lucknow's worst 2024 defeat was Lost by 98 runs. But the margin has been negative in three straight seasons.

counter.q: Does the outlook (ninth, 28%) agree with the record?
counter.a: Broadly yes. It rates the bowling late overs highly and the powerplay badly, which differs from the record's weakness at the death. The two views do not agree on where the problem lies.

counter.q: Is one season of 4 wins in 13 enough to judge?
counter.a: It is a small sample, but the run totals agree with the table.

implications: Add a wicket-taker for the late overs: Lucknow take the fewest wickets at the death in the league.
Fix the powerplay on both sides: the bowling concedes 1.2 runs a match more than the league and the batting scores 2.2 fewer.
Rebuild the plan for batting first, which used to be the strength.
deep.verdict: Lucknow's decline is real in the run totals, spread across bowling phases, and sharpest in the late overs. It is solvable, with a bowling plan rather than a rebuild.

cases.headline: Fast starts, loose finishes
cases.dek: The best powerplay batting in the league and the worst death bowling, with the most extras given away at the end.
cases.question: Rajasthan top the league in the powerplay and bottom it in the death. Where does the game get lost?

evidence.title: A powerplay powerhouse
evidence.body: The outlook rates Rajasthan's powerplay batting 6.9 out of 10, among the highest batting scores in the league.

evidence.title: A leaking finish
evidence.body: Death bowling rates 2.5, the lowest rating of any unit in the league, and the powerplay bowling is also weak (3.9).

evidence.title: The extras problem
evidence.body: Rajasthan's likely death bowlers concede 0.52 wides and no-ball runs per over at the death, against a league rate of 0.37, the worst in the league. In the historical data, extras at the death cost teams more than their run value alone.

evidence.title: Last year's swing
evidence.body: After -33 in 2025 (a 31% win rate), the side rebounded to +5 and made the playoffs in 2026. A typical team's strength moves about 18 runs a match from the league average, so a swing of 38 is large but not unheard of.

cases.insight: Rajasthan show how to read a ranking critically: the lowest overall position hides one elite phase and one serious red flag. The most practical lever is not a new star; it is a bowling plan that moves the weakest death overs onto the most disciplined hands.
watch: Which two bowlers take the death overs, and their extras record
The use of spin at the death
Whether the top order keeps the powerplay edge against better new-ball bowling
cases.takeaway: Tenth on paper, with a fixable weakness.

deep.short_answer: Rajasthan's powerplay batting is genuinely one of the league's best, and their death-over bowling is genuinely one of its worst, with the most extras given away. Both show in five seasons of ball-by-ball data.
deep.why: A ranking's overall number hides where a team wins and loses. Rajasthan show how one elite phase and one weak one can cancel.

analysis.title: A powerplay batting edge that is real
analysis.simple: Runs per over against the league over 2024 to 2026; the powerplay is overs 1 to 6.
body: Rajasthan's powerplay batting scored 10.40 an over against 9.74, about 3.9 runs a match more (rank 2 of 10), with 29% of balls going for four or six against 26%.

analysis.title: The most extras in the league

analysis.title: 2025 was the outlier
analysis.simple: Run margin per match, scored minus conceded.
body: In 2025 Rajasthan scored 185.8 and conceded 198.8, a margin of -13.0, and won 4 of 13 (chasing 2 from 9). The runs point to 4.8 wins, so that season was as bad as it looked.

analysis.title: The bounce back
analysis.simple: Win rate and net run rate in 2026.
body: In 2026 Rajasthan won 8 of 14 with a net run rate of +0.28, scoring 187.1 and conceding 189.2. V Suryavanshi made 583 runs and JC Archer took 21 wickets at 8.77 an over.

history: 2022: 9 wins and a net run rate of +0.27. 2023: 7 wins, +0.55, a season that included a 112-run defeat.
2024: 8 wins and a net run rate of +0.27, with a chase record of 6 from 8.
2025: 4 wins, net run rate −0.42. 2026: 8 wins, +0.28.

Bowled out for 59 in 2023, with five wickets lost in the powerplay.
A 72-run win in 2023 with a powerplay of 85 for 1.

hidden.title: The extras sit with some bowlers
body: In 2026 JC Archer took 15 death overs at 8.73 an over with 0.27 extras an over. Sandeep Sharma went for 13.70 an over.

hidden.title: Top-heavy, less than before
body: In 2024 the top three scored 62% of the team's runs; in 2026 it was 57%, against a league average of 54%.

counter.q: Could the extras figure be a small-sample result?
counter.a: The death-over figure rests on a few bowlers, and extras are noisy from one season to the next. The three-season average is the fairer read.

counter.q: Does a powerplay edge win matches?
counter.a: It helps, but Rajasthan's record does not show it dominating: their run margins have been small.

counter.q: Is the outlook's 10th place too harsh?
counter.a: The record has been mid-table by runs. The outlook rates the death bowling as weakest in the league, which the record supports.

implications: Move the death overs to the bowlers with the best discipline: extras run from 0.27 to 0.72 an over inside one attack.
Protect the powerplay: it is worth about 3.9 runs a match against the league.
Add a reliable second death option; one wicket-taker cannot cover five overs.
deep.verdict: Rajasthan are mid-table by the runs, with an elite first six overs and a poor last five. The overall rank understates how fixable that is.

cases.headline: A year up, a year down, a bowling edge in the powerplay
cases.dek: Sunrisers' strength has alternated sign in each of the last five seasons.
cases.question: Does a team that alternates between good and bad years have a predictable shape?

evidence.title: Up, down, up, down, up

evidence.title: The strongest powerplay bowling in the league

evidence.title: A second discipline flag
evidence.body: Sunrisers' likely death bowlers concede 0.46 extras per over at the death, the second-worst rate in the league, behind only Rajasthan.

cases.insight: Sunrisers are built to win the first six overs of the bowling innings and to coast through the rest. The batting at the death and the bowling in the middle overs are the two phases a rival would target, and the extras at the death are the discipline question behind them.

cases.headline: Second in the outlook, last in playoff trips
cases.dek: Three playoff appearances in nineteen seasons, and a squad the outlook rates among the best.
cases.question: How does a franchise with no title and three playoff appearances end up second in a squad ranking?

evidence.title: The franchise record
evidence.body: Three playoffs in nineteen seasons (including as Kings XI Punjab), no titles, the lowest count of the eight long-running franchises.

evidence.title: A recent step up
evidence.body: 2025 was +12 with a 69% win rate and a playoff place. 2026 was +0.3 with a 54% win rate, and Punjab missed the playoffs.

evidence.title: What the outlook sees

evidence.title: Why the history does not enter
evidence.body: The outlook looks at the players, not the franchise name. That is exactly right when the squad has really changed, and a risk when the dressing-room context matters more than the numbers show.

cases.insight: Punjab is the case that most tests how a ranking should be read: the squad is rated far better than the franchise's record. A reasonable analyst reads the 47% as 'a good squad with a thin track record', not as a prediction that the history is over.

Whether the death-batting strength comes from one or two players
How the side handles pressure games, which the data cannot measure
cases.takeaway: A squad-level case for optimism, and a record that urges caution.

deep.short_answer: Punjab's recent run totals are good, led by the second-best death-over batting in the league, but their bowling at the death is poor. The squad is stronger than the franchise's history of three playoff places suggests.
deep.why: A franchise's history and its current squad can tell different stories. The ball-by-ball record shows which one the recent play supports.

analysis.title: A better record than the run totals
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from runs scored and conceded.
body: In 2025 Punjab won 9 of 13 against 7.1 expected. In 2026 they scored 208.5 and conceded 209.1, a margin of -0.6, and won 7 of 13.

analysis.title: A chasing side
analysis.simple: Win rate when chasing compared with batting first.
body: In 2026 Punjab won 6 of 8 chases and 1 of 5 batting first. Over five seasons: 61% chasing and 40% batting first.

analysis.title: Spread across the order
analysis.simple: Share of the team's runs scored by the top three.
body: In 2026 the top three (P Simran Singh, SS Iyer, C Connolly) scored 58% of the team's runs, about the league level of 54%.

history: 2022 to 2024: 7, 6 and 5 wins, all with net run rates close to zero (+0.11, −0.24, −0.22).
2025: 9 wins, net run rate +0.34.
2026: 7 wins, net run rate +0.31, and 208.5 runs a match scored, the most of their last five seasons.

matches.why: 116 for 0 in the powerplay and a successful chase of 265 in 2026: Simran Singh 76 off 26.
A 60-run defeat in 2024: Bengaluru scored 77 for 4 in the death overs.

matches.venue: Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium
matches.why: A two-run defeat in 2024 after Shashank Singh's 46 off 25. Arshdeep took 4 for 29.

matches.note: Fewest runs conceded in a full set of death overs since 2022
matches.why: Punjab held Delhi to 21 for 2 in the death overs in 2023, their tightest death-over defence of the five seasons.

hidden.title: The franchise history does not enter the numbers
body: Punjab have three playoff places in 19 seasons, but their 2025 and 2026 run totals are good. The outlook's second place is a squad judgment, not a history one.

hidden.title: Arshdeep's death overs have worsened
body: Arshdeep Singh conceded 11.77 an over in the death overs in 2026 with 0.85 extras an over, against 9.59 in 2025.

counter.q: Is the batting a product of high-scoring grounds?
counter.a: Possibly: Punjab played at several venues, and our data does not adjust for them.

counter.q: Is the squad's strength a thin foundation?
counter.a: The franchise record is thin, and the data cannot predict pressure moments.

counter.q: Does a chasing record last?
counter.a: Over five seasons it has been 61%, but one season's 6 from 8 is a small sample.

implications: Fix the death-over bowling: it concedes 2.9 runs a match more than the league, the main cost against a very strong batting finish.
Plan for batting first: the 2026 record was 1 from 5.
Keep the death-batting core: it adds 4.3 runs a match.
deep.verdict: Punjab have a squad that scores heavily at the finish, a bowling unit that does not defend, and a franchise history that urges caution. A good outlook with a clear weakness.
deep.data_note: League-stage IPL matches only (playoffs excluded). Team and player figures use 2022 to 2026; the expected-wins fit uses every season since 2008 (153 team-seasons). Phase comparisons use the last three seasons, 2024 to 2026. Close matches are those decided by 10 runs or fewer, or 2 wickets or fewer.

cases.headline: A strong middle-over attack and nothing at the edges
cases.dek: Six playoffs in nineteen seasons, no titles, and a squad built for one phase of the game.
cases.question: What does a team that is neither good nor bad actually look like in the data?

evidence.title: The same story every year
evidence.body: Delhi's season strength reads +6, -31, -11, -1, -11 over the last five years, with a win rate of exactly 50% in four of them. They have not reached the playoffs in that time.

evidence.title: One elite phase
evidence.body: Bowling in the middle overs rates 7.7 out of 10, the third-highest unit rating in the league. Axar Patel, Starc and Chameera are in StatEdge's XI.

evidence.title: Weak where games are decided early
evidence.body: Powerplay bowling (3.6) and powerplay batting (3.9) are both in the bottom three of the league.

evidence.title: Top-heavy again
evidence.body: The top three batters score about 56% of the team's runs, the second-highest share in the league, behind only Gujarat.

cases.insight: Delhi's problem is that its strength is concentrated in the phase where the game is least often won. A middle-over specialist attack is valuable, but if the powerplay on both sides goes against them, the middle overs are played from behind. The data suggests the best use of resources is a powerplay bowler, not more depth in the phase that already works.
watch: The identity of the powerplay bowling pair
Whether the top three keep carrying the batting
The impact player: a powerplay bowler on the bench could change the plan
cases.takeaway: A well-built middle with nothing on either side.

deep.short_answer: Delhi have finished above their run totals in all five seasons. Their .500 records flatter them. Their bowling is average, not elite, in the middle overs, and weak in the powerplay.
deep.why: A team that is always middling is easy to dismiss. Looking at the margin shows how much of the middle was luck.

analysis.title: Always above what the runs say
analysis.simple: Expected wins estimate how many games a team should win from runs scored and conceded.
body: From 2022 to 2026 Delhi won 32 of 68 league games against 27.8 expected, a gap of 4.2 wins in their favour. They finished above expectation in all 5 of the five seasons.
In 2023 they scored 155.9 a match and conceded 173.1, a margin of -17.2, the weakest in the data for them, and won 5 of 14.

analysis.title: Neither half of the record is strong
analysis.simple: Win rate when chasing compared with batting first. League-wide, chasing teams win 56%.
body: Delhi won 19 of 42 chases (45%) and 13 of 26 batting first (50%). In 2026 they won 6 of 9 chasing and 1 of 5 batting first, so the 2026 split looked unlike the five-season one.

analysis.title: Powerplay on both sides is the problem
analysis.simple: Runs a match against the league over 2024 to 2026. Positive on the bowling side means worse than the league.
body: Delhi's powerplay bowling conceded 10.26 an over against 9.74, about 3.1 runs a match more than the league, and they take only 39% dots against 42%. Their powerplay batting scored 1.2 runs a match fewer than the league and lost 5.2 wickets per 100 balls against 4.3.

analysis.title: Middle-over bowling is average in the record
analysis.simple: Runs per over in the middle overs, 7 to 15.
body: Delhi conceded 9.08 an over in the middle overs against 9.09, almost exactly the league average. The 2027 outlook rates this unit as the third strongest in the league, which the last three seasons do not show.

analysis.title: One batter makes the difference
analysis.simple: Share of the team's runs scored by one player.
body: In 2026 KL Rahul made 593 runs at a strike rate of 174, 24% of the team's total. The next two, P Nissanka and T Stubbs, made 278 and 275.

history: 2022: 7 wins and a net run rate of +0.27. 2023: 5 wins and −0.80, the weakest margin of the five.
2024: 7 wins and −0.31; they won both of their close matches. 2025: 6 wins and +0.07.
2026: 7 wins and −0.63, 6.8 expected.

matches.venue: Andhra Cricket Association-Visakhapatnam District Cricket Association Stadium
matches.why: A 106-run defeat to Kolkata in 2024: 272 for 7, with 88 for 1 in the powerplay.
A one-run defeat to Gujarat in 2026 despite 92 from KL Rahul and 209 on the board.
A four-run win in 2024: Pant 88 off 43 and 97 for 1 in the death overs.
92 for 0 in the powerplay and 257 in 2024. Fraser-McGurk made 84 off 27. A reminder of what the batting can do when the top order goes.

hidden.title: The outlook and the record disagree about the middle-over bowling
body: The outlook credits Delhi's middle-over bowling as a strength, and the last three seasons show it at the league average. It may reflect the current squad (Axar Patel, Starc and Chameera), but the data cannot confirm it.

hidden.title: Death bowling depends on one man
body: In 2026 L Ngidi bowled 17 death overs at 8.31 an over. Mukesh Kumar went for 12.14, and in 2025 Mukesh Kumar conceded 15.39 an over.

counter.q: Is finishing above expectation five years running a skill?
counter.a: It could be: close matches and chases are partly skill. Delhi's close record is small (5 from 8), so we cannot say.

counter.q: Is the powerplay problem fixable?
counter.a: The data cannot say. The batting and bowling powerplay problems come from different squads and different seasons.

counter.q: Does the outlook's sixth place make sense?
counter.a: The record says Delhi are weaker than their wins. The outlook is generous to the middle-over bowling.

implications: Invest in a powerplay bowler: it concedes 3.1 runs a match more than the league.
Do not rely on the middle-over bowling until it shows in the results.
Look at chasing: 45% over five seasons against a league rate of 56%.
deep.verdict: Delhi are a weaker team than their records, with one star batter and weak powerplays on both sides. Mid-table is generous.

glossary.term: Runs per innings above or below the league
glossary.meaning: How many runs more or fewer than an average team a side scores (or concedes) in a phase of one innings. We turn a runs-per-over gap into runs per innings so it can be felt: 0.5 runs an over across the six powerplay overs is 3 runs.

A fair estimate of how many games a team should have won from the runs it scored and conceded, fitted on every IPL season since 2008. If wins run well above or below it, the record flatters or hides the team.
Runs scored per over minus runs conceded per over across a season. The IPL uses it to break ties on points.
How many runs a match a team is above or below the league's average team that season, counting both runs and wickets in each phase. Strength is what the 2027 outlook ranks.
The share of a team's runs scored by its three highest run-scorers. A high share means the order is top-heavy.
An index of 100 means better than almost every comparable player. The range shows where the true value probably sits; a wide range means a small sample.
Decided by 10 runs or fewer, or by 2 wickets or fewer. Results in close matches are close to coin flips.
